::: {#brief .lx-sec}
```{=html}
<div class="lx-card lx-cap-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The brief</p>
<p class="lx-case-q">What should one site install behind its meter: the Prairie Town home, or the ridge wind farm? You advise its owner.</p>
<ol class="lx-studio-task">
<li><b>Start from:</b> the owner's goal, in one line: the most money over the plan's life, or less CO₂ at a cost you state. Either can pass, with its trade-off in numbers.</li>
<li><b>Hand in:</b> a plan link and a one-page note; its sensitivity part lists every bar of the chart in numbers (Modeler version: one M4 comparison too).</li>
<li><b>From:</b> the <a href="sb0-site-bench.html">Site Bench</a>'s engine, below, with every hour of 2025: solar, a battery and a <span class="lx-term" data-term="heat-pump">heat pump</span>, or an <span class="lx-term" data-term="electrolyzer">electrolyzer</span> and a hydrogen tank.</li>
<li><b>Done when:</b> every check under the note is in place, and your note meets each "Look for" line of the self-check.</li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-hint">About 60 minutes: 25 to build and test the plan, 25 to write the note, 10 to check it.</p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#note .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## Write your one-page note
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-card c0-yard">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Before you write: which number defends the plan?</p>
<p>On the wind farm, the bench shows two numbers that can disagree: the cost per kg of hydrogen, and what the extra equipment adds to the <span class="lx-term" data-term="net-present-value">NPV</span>.</p>
<blockquote class="lx-excerpt" data-source="excerpt:wind-hydrogen"><p>As the hydrogen price rose, the optimizer built a larger electrolyzer to use more surplus wind.</p><p>The larger unit ran at lower utilization, so each kilogram carried more capital and the <span class="lx-term" data-term="lcoh">levelized cost of hydrogen</span> rose, while hydrogen revenue lowered total system cost.</p><footer>Approved excerpt of: Li et al. (2024), <a href="https://doi.org/10.1115/1.4063971">Journal of Mechanical Design</a>.</footer></blockquote>
<blockquote class="lx-excerpt" data-source="excerpt:solar-hydrogen"><p>Among the cases studied, <span class="lx-term" data-term="concentrated-solar">concentrated solar power</span> with <span class="lx-term" data-term="thermal-storage">thermal storage</span> running a <span class="lx-term" data-term="high-temperature-electrolyzer">high-temperature electrolyzer</span> at variable power gave the lowest levelized cost of hydrogen; constant-power operation was the most expensive.</p><footer>Approved excerpt of: Li et al. (2023), <a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/EEM58374.2023.10161786">EEM 2023</a>.</footer></blockquote>
<p class="lx-hint">Yardstick here: the cost per kilogram across designs. Holds for: one West Texas site, cost projections from NREL's Annual Technology Baseline, a conference-length study.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Say which yardstick your note uses. <a href="cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.html">Case file CF2</a> takes the first case apart.</p>
</div>
<div id="c0-note" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- c0-note:start (written by LX.ReportNote.outlineHTML from the page's fields in the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<ol class="lx-rn-outline"><li><b>Title and plan link:</b> the plan's link from the bench, and the date</li><li><b>Recommendation:</b> Two sentences: the owner's goal, what this site should install or not, and the number that decides it.</li><li><b>The plan:</b> each choice, with its unit</li><li><b>Results:</b> each result, with its unit and boundary</li><li><b>Assumptions:</b> one sentence each</li><li><b>Sensitivity:</b> every bar of the sensitivity chart in numbers, and what was held fixed</li><li><b>What the site cannot do alone:</b> One or two sentences: what it still needs from the grid or a buyer, and when.</li><li><b>What would change the answer:</b> One sentence from your sensitivity chart: does any tested input change the recommendation, and between which values?</li><li><b>Limits of this analysis:</b> what the model leaves out</li></ol>
<!-- c0-note:end -->
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The Modeler version: one comparison from the M4 notebook</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- Storage and coupled carriers, modelling power, hydrogen and heat together ([M4](m04-storage-multienergy.html), in the Modeler tier), writes a plant [linear program]{.lx-term term="linear-program"} like the bench's in Python.
- It is another plant: two weeks, power bought and sold, a fixed hydrogen demand and a heat store; it has no NPV.
- Hand in, with the note: the notebook's weekly saving from adding the electrolyzer and tank (its section 3), winter and summer.
- Then two sentences: how its model differs from the bench's, and which difference could change your recommendation.
- About 45 minutes. Work through [M4](m04-storage-multienergy.html) first; [B3](b03-read-check-formulation.html) shows how to read a formulation in words.
